title: Distilling Literary Sentiment from LLM Annotations into an Ordinal BERT Model
abstract: arXiv:2611.02985v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The scarcity of human-annotated literary corpora limits the development of domain-specific sentiment analysis models. This study investigates whether LLM-generated annotations can supervise smaller models for literary sentiment analysis. We fine-tune five BERT models using ordinal regression on 10,889 literary sentences annotated by Gemma 4 31B on a ten-point sentiment scale. The models are evaluated against 1,923 human-annotated sentences from Hemingway's "The Old Man and the Sea", alongside the teacher model and conventional baselines.   BERT-large achieves a Kendall's $\tau$ of 0.589, approaching the teacher's 0.604. Although a constant-neutral predictor achieves the lowest overall mean absolute error (MAE), BERT-base outperforms the teacher on non-neutral sentences, achieving an MAE of 0.726 versus 1.116. translated_title: 将大语言模型标注中的文学情感蒸馏到序数BERT模型中
translated_abstract: 人工标注文学语料的稀缺性限制了领域特定情感分析模型的发展。本研究探讨由大语言模型生成的标注是否能够监督较小的模型进行文学情感分析。我们在10,889条由Gemma 4 31B在十分制情感量表上标注的文学句子上，使用序数回归方法微调了五个BERT模型。这些模型在海明威《老人与海》的1,923条人工标注句子上进行评估，并与教师模型及传统基线方法进行比较。BERT-large取得了0.589的Kendall's τ，接近教师模型的0.604。尽管恒定中性预测器实现了最低的总体平均绝对误差（MAE），但BERT-base在非中性句子上的表现优于教师模型，MAE为0.726，而教师模型为1.116。这些发现证明了大语言模型生成监督在开发更小型文学情感模型方面的潜力。
tldr: 本研究利用Gemma 4 31B生成的标注通过序数回归蒸馏训练小型BERT模型进行文学情感分析，其中BERT-large的性能接近教师模型，且BERT-base在非中性句子上的表现甚至超越了教师模型。
en_tdlr: This study distills LLM-generated annotations from Gemma 4 31B into smaller BERT models via ordinal regression for literary sentiment analysis, with BERT-large approaching teacher-level performance and BERT-base even outperforming the teacher on non-neutral sentences.
